text:
Facets
lemma_facets drops any lemma the surface index already holds, meaning one whose fold_token matches the surface form.
A source may already carry the analysis. etym_facets reads the > etym: lines a reader wrote and splits them by script: a token with Devanagari or IAST diacritics is a lemma, a plain English word is a gloss. source_meta is metre plus timings plus that, and it is what sanskrit_meta(None) returns — no vidyut import, no 81 MB download. When a pipeline is supplied, the source’s own analysis still wins and vidyut is called only for the chunks that lack one.

def lemma_facets(
    text:str, # chunk text
    nlp, # a `vidyut_pipe()` (or any spaCy-shaped pipeline)
    max_terms:int=96, # cap, so one chunk's metadata cannot outgrow its content

{'lemma': 'gam vac ...'} for a chunk — the dictionary forms behind its inflected words.



from ganapati.text import vr_xml_parse


VR = '''<lyrics><section name="anuvaka 1">
  <line ignore="true">॥ श्रीरुद्रचमकप्रश्नः ॥</line>
  <line start_time_ms="0" end_time_ms="1800"
        etymology="agni: fire, the god of fire; viṣṇu: voc. du., the all-pervader">अग्नाविष्णू सजोषसेमा</line>
</section></lyrics>'''

f = etym_facets(vr_xml_parse(VR)[0][-1][1])
assert f['lemma'] == 'agni viṣṇu'                        # the headword of each `word: gloss` entry
assert f['gloss'] == 'fire god all-pervader'             # and no grammar, no stopwords
assert sanskrit_meta() is source_meta                    # the cheap path, and no vidyut in it
assert source_meta(vr_xml_parse(VR)[0][-1][1])['mora_rate'] == '112'

text:
Profiles
register_profiles() tells litesearch which extensions to try, how to sniff a shared one, which chunker, and what metadata to write. It runs on import. Call it again with nlp= and mw= to add lemmas and glosses to everything indexed after.


source

register_profiles
def register_profiles(
    nlp:NoneType=None, mw:dict=None
):
Register the Sanskrit profiles. Called on import; safe to call again.



from litesearch.data import profile_for
from litesearch import Index
import json, numpy as np
from fastcore.all import Path, first


gretil = "atha prathamo'dhyāyaḥ || MBh_1,1.1 ||\n" * 10
p = profile_for('mahabharata_u.htm', gretil)
assert p and p.name == 'sanskrit_verse'
assert p.chunker is VerseChunker and p.kind == 'sanskrit'

assert sanskrit_meta(None) is source_meta          # no pipeline, no vidyut import
# and it still carries the metre: a real verse in, its metre out
assert sanskrit_meta(None)('dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ '
                          'māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāścaiva kimakurvata sañjaya')['meter'] == 'anuṣṭubh'
assert sanskrit_meta(None)('') == {}


# the corpus's own shape: `surface, lemma, grammar…, gloss`, one entry per line
E = """> etym: गणानां, gaṇa, genitive case, masculine gender, plural number, of troops.
> etym: हवामहे, hvā, present tense, indicative mood, first person, plural number, we invoke.
> etym: विष्णुं, viṣṇu, case=accusative, gender=masculine, number=singular, Viṣṇu, the object of the meditation."""
f = etym_facets(E)
assert 'gaṇa' in f['lemma'] and 'hvā' in f['lemma'] and 'गणानां' in f['lemma']
# the grammar fields go to neither side: the lemma already implies them
assert 'troops' in f['gloss'] and 'invoke' in f['gloss']
assert not {'genitive', 'masculine', 'plural', 'accusative', 'tense', 'case'} & set(f['gloss'].split())

# the two other shapes a source may use still split
assert 'agnā' in etym_facets('> etym: agnā: agni, voc. du.')['lemma']
assert 'dharma' in etym_facets('> etym: The compound joins dharma with kshetra.')['gloss']


# the same lines read as records: surface, lemma, the grammar fields, the gloss
es = etym_entries('गणानां, gaṇa, genitive case, masculine gender, plural number, of troops.\n'
                  'विष्णुं, viṣṇu, case=accusative, gender=masculine, number=singular, Viṣṇu, the object of the meditation.\n'
                  'तत्, tad, nominal stem, form of the pronoun, that.\n'
                  '- agnā: agni, voc. du.')            # a `word: gloss` bullet is the other shape, not an entry
assert len(es) == 3
assert es[0].w == 'गणानां' and es[0].lemma == 'gaṇa' and es[0].gram == 'genitive case, masculine gender, plural number' and es[0].g == 'of troops.'
assert es[1].gram == 'case=accusative, gender=masculine, number=singular' and es[1].g == 'Viṣṇu, the object of the meditation.'
assert es[2].gram == 'nominal stem, form of the pronoun' and es[2].g == 'that.'   # a gloss with a comma in it stays whole
assert etym_entries('') == [] and etym_entries('just prose, with commas, in it') == []

section: A gloss that was written in the wrong script
text:
A gloss that was written in the wrong script
An LLM asked for a Devanagari headword sometimes reads the English gloss as IAST and writes it in Devanagari too, so an ox; cattle becomes अन् ओक्ष्; चत्त्ले. delatinize reads such a line back. The reference is the corpus’s own vocabulary, gloss_vocab, so a word only counts as English when the corpus has glossed with it before; a well-formed entry and a real Sanskrit line are left alone. Reading back needs aksharamukha, which is not a dependency: the first call says so.

delatinize

    s:str, vocab:set
)->str:
A mis-transliterated English gloss read back; a well-formed entry or real Sanskrit is returned as it came.

latin_frac

    s:str, # one Devanagari line
    vocab:set, # the corpus's English gloss words, from `gloss_vocab`
    scheme:str='IAST'

How much of a line reads back as English, as (fraction, n_words). Multi-word runs only: one surface word proves nothing.

gloss_vocab
def gloss_vocab(
    texts
)->set:
The English words the corpus’s own parseable glosses use: the reference for spotting an entry that is not English at all.



v = gloss_vocab(['गणानां, gaṇa, genitive case, of troops.',
                 'गौः, go, nominative case, an ox; cattle; the earth.',
                 'सूर्यः, sūrya, nominative case, the sun; light of the sun.'])
assert v == {'an', 'cattle', 'earth', 'light', 'of', 'ox', 'sun', 'the', 'troops'}

bad = 'थे सुन्; लिघ्त् ओफ़् थे सुन्'                  # `the sun; light of the sun`, written as if it were IAST
assert latin_frac(bad, v) == (1.0, 6)
assert delatinize(bad, v) == 'the sun; light of the sun'

# left alone: real Sanskrit, a well-formed entry, a header, a `word: gloss` bullet
for s in ['गणानां त्वा गणपतिं हवामहे', 'गणानां, gaṇa, genitive case, of troops.', 'ॐ भूः', '- ॐ: Sacred syllable', '']:
    assert delatinize(s, v) == s
assert latin_frac('गणानां त्वा गणपतिं हवामहे', v) == (0.0, 4)

t, n = fix_etym(f'ॐ भूः\n{bad}\nगणानां, gaṇa, genitive case, of troops.', v)
assert n == 1 and t.splitlines()[1] == 'the sun; light of the sun' and t.splitlines()[0] == 'ॐ भूः'


# a real numbered HTML edition follows the same profile through Index.add.
# `mahabharata.htm` is GRETIL's Mahābhārata 1.1, 210 verses:

title: text
text:
Three markers, tried in order of how much they say:

a citation, // Mn_1.1 //, which is also a stable id
a Devanagari verse number, ॥ १॥
a daṇḍa at end of line

A cut swallows the > gloss lines trailing it, so a translation stays with its verse.


source


def verse_spans(
    text:str
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Split text into verse units, returning (start, end, text, citation).



from ganapati.text import cite_parts, verse_spans


assert cite_parts('BrhUp_1,1.2') == ('BrhUp', ['1','1','2'])
assert cite_parts('Mn_1.1') == ('Mn', ['1','1'])
assert cite_parts('IsUp_4[57M]') == ('IsUp', ['4'])      # the alternate-edition number is dropped
assert cite_parts('not a citation') == ('not a citation', [])

two = ('īśā vāsyam idaṃ sarvaṃ | tena tyaktena bhuñjīthāḥ || IsUp_1 ||\n'
       'kurvann eveha karmāṇi | evaṃ tvayi nānyatheto || IsUp_2 ||\n')
sp = verse_spans(two)
assert len(sp) == 2
assert [c for *_, c in sp] == ['IsUp_1', 'IsUp_2']
assert sp[0][2].startswith('īśā') and sp[0][2].endswith('||')

numbered = ('0nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya\n'
            '  1\n'
            'lomaharṣaṇaputra ugraśravāḥ\n'
            '2samāsīnān abhyagacchat')
sp = verse_spans(numbered)
assert len(sp) == 3
assert [s for *_, s, _ in sp] == [
    'nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya', 'lomaharṣaṇaputra ugraśravāḥ', 'samāsīnān abhyagacchat']

title: text
text:
Words and pādas
A recitation source hands over a verse as one line with its number glued on; the reader wants one pāda per line and the number in Devanagari. These are the cuts, so nobody redefines a daṇḍa.


source

padas
def padas(
    verse:str, # one verse, on one line or several, with or without its end-marker
    num:NoneType=None, # the verse number to close it with; None keeps the one the verse carries
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
A verse as pāda lines: cut at the daṇḍa, a glued …उवाच speaker tag on its own line first, the last line closed with ॥ num ॥.




source

split_mantras
def split_mantras(
    text:str
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
A text blob as (number, body) pairs, cut at its ॥ n ॥ end-markers, the number as written.

deva_num

    n
)->str:
A verse number in Devanagari digits: 18 -> १८, 1.1 -> १.१.




source

is_word
def is_word(
    t:str
)->bool:
A token with a letter in it: a daṇḍa, a verse number or a lone punctuation mark is not a word.



from ganapati.text import is_word, deva_num, split_mantras, padas


assert is_word('धर्मक्षेत्रे') and is_word('kṣetre') and is_word('yuyutsavaḥ,')
assert not is_word('॥') and not is_word('।') and not is_word('१८') and not is_word('1.1') and not is_word('')
assert deva_num(18) == '१८' and deva_num('1.1') == '१.१'

# Gītā 1.1 as DharmicData prints it: one line, the speaker glued on, the chapter.verse marker at the end
g11 = 'धृतराष्ट्र उवाच धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः । मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ।। 1.1 ।।'
assert padas(g11, 1) == ['धृतराष्ट्र उवाच', 'धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।', 'मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥ १ ॥']
assert padas(g11)[-1].endswith('॥ १.१ ॥')             # no number given: the one the verse carries, in Devanagari
assert padas('मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय')[-1].endswith(' ॥')   # no number anywhere: a bare close

# Kumārasambhava 4.1 across two lines with its own daṇḍas: the lines are only re-cut
K41 = 'अथ मोहपरायणा सती विवशा कामवधूर्विबोधिता ।\nविधिना प्रतिपादयिष्यता नववैधव्यमसह्यवेदनम् ॥'
assert padas(K41, 1) == ['अथ मोहपरायणा सती विवशा कामवधूर्विबोधिता ।', 'विधिना प्रतिपादयिष्यता नववैधव्यमसह्यवेदनम् ॥ १ ॥']

# a saṃhitā blob: two mantras, numbered as written, each then split into its pādas
blob = 'इषे त्वोर्जे त्वा वायव स्थ देवो वः सविता प्रार्पयतु ॥ १ ॥ वसोः पवित्रमसि शतधारं । वसोः पवित्रमसि सहस्रधारम् ॥ २ ॥'
ms = split_mantras(blob)
assert [n for n, _ in ms] == ['१', '२'] and ms[0][1].startswith('इषे')
assert padas(ms[1][1], ms[1][0]) == ['वसोः पवित्रमसि शतधारं ।', 'वसोः पवित्रमसि सहस्रधारम् ॥ २ ॥']
assert split_mantras('') == [] and padas('') == []

# DharmicData prints AV 2.36.7's close as `॥७` with no closing daṇḍa and a newline: still a verse end, or 7 merges into 8 and `७` is left glued mid-line
av = 'अन्यं वेत्तवे ॥७\nआ ते नयतु सविता ॥ ८ ॥'
assert split_mantras(av) == [('७', 'अन्यं वेत्तवे'), ('८', 'आ ते नयतु सविता')]
assert padas('अन्यं वेत्तवे ॥७') == ['अन्यं वेत्तवे ॥ ७ ॥']
assert split_mantras('क । १० ख ॥ ११ ॥') == [('११', 'क । १० ख')]                 # a number after a daṇḍa mid-line is text, not a marker

# a paryāya sūkta (AV 16.8) writes a running count after the marker, `॥४॥ ४। १`: a single daṇḍa before a bare number is not a marker
py = 'पादयामि॥४॥ ४। १\nजितमस्माकम्॥१॥'
assert split_mantras(py) == [('४', 'पादयामि'), ('१', '४। १\nजितमस्माकम्')]

# the speaker tag is cut only where `वाच` ends the word: Chāndogya 4.2.3's `प्रत्युवाचाह` goes on, and so do `वाचं`, `वाचः`, `वाचा`
ch = 'तमु ह परः प्रत्युवाचाह हारेत्वा शूद्र तवैव सह गोभिरस्त्विति ।'
assert padas(ch) == ['तमु ह परः प्रत्युवाचाह हारेत्वा शूद्र तवैव सह गोभिरस्त्विति ॥']
assert padas('श्रीभगवानुवाच कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् ।')[:2] == ['श्रीभगवानुवाच', 'कुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् ॥']
assert padas(g11)[0] == 'धृतराष्ट्र उवाच' and padas('अर्जुन उवाच ।') == ['अर्जुन उवाच']
for w in ('गुरुवाचं श्रुत्वा', 'तदुवाचः स आह', 'मधुवाचा वदति', 'अनुवाचम् इति'): assert padas(w) == [f'{w} ॥'], w

# DharmicData glues 11 Gītā speaker tags to the pāda with no space (12.1, 12.2, 13.2, 14.1, 14.21, 14.22, 15.1, 17.1, 17.2, 18.73, 18.74): a letter after `वाच` starts the pāda
glued = [
    ('अर्जुन उवाचएवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते।येचाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः।।12.1।।', 1, ['अर्जुन उवाच', 'एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते ।', 'येचाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः ॥ १ ॥']),
    ('श्री भगवानुवाचमय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते।श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः।।12.2।।', 2, ['श्री भगवानुवाच', 'मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते ।', 'श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः ॥ २ ॥']),
    ('श्री भगवानुवाचइदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते।एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः।।13.2।।', 2, ['श्री भगवानुवाच', 'इदं शरीरं कौन्तेय क्षेत्रमित्यभिधीयते ।', 'एतद्यो वेत्ति तं प्राहुः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति तद्विदः ॥ २ ॥']),

Chunkers
VerseChunker is chonkie-shaped and drops into add_doc(chunker=...). It cuts on verse boundaries, packs short verses towards target, and splits long prose at max_chars. ProseChunker is the same with a bigger budget and pack_cited=True.

    target:int=700, max_chars:int=1400, pack_cited:bool=True

VerseChunker tuned for Sanskrit prose — commentary, bhāṣya, the prose Upaniṣads.




source

VerseChunker
def VerseChunker(
    target:int=300, max_chars:int=900, pack_cited:bool=False
):
A chonkie-shaped chunker whose cuts land on verse boundaries.




source

chunk_verses
def chunk_verses(
    text:str, # source text
    target:int=300, # pack short units forward up to this many chars
    max_chars:int=900, # split a unit longer than this at clause boundaries
    pack_cited:bool=False, # let consecutive cited units share a chunk up to `target`
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
Verse-aware chunks: cut on citation/daṇḍa, pack short units, split long prose.



from litesearch.tree import _pack_target


cs = VerseChunker().chunk(two)
assert len(cs) == 2
assert two[cs[0].start_index:cs[0].end_index] == cs[0].text   # offsets point back at the source

# ProseChunker packs cited units instead, which is what commentary wants
assert len(ProseChunker().chunk(two)) == 1

# with no citation to cut on, the budget decides. 3,040 characters of daṇḍa-separated prose:
long = ' | '.join(['padam yatra tatra sarvatra gacchati'] * 80) + ' ||'
assert len(chunk_verses(long, 300, 900)) == 4
assert len(chunk_verses(long, 700, 1400)) == 3

# litesearch packs across segments only for a chunker that asks; the verse profile does not,
# because a reader that emits one verse per page is already the right size
assert _pack_target(VerseChunker()) == 0
assert _pack_target(ProseChunker()) == 700

VR = """<lyrics>
  <category>vedic</category><tags>rudram</tags>
  <section name="title">
    <line ignore="true">॥ श्रीरुद्रचमकप्रश्नः ॥</line>
  </section>
  <section name="anuvaka 1" meaning="A dual invocation of Agni and Viṣṇu.">
    <line start_time_ms="0" end_time_ms="1800" alignment_id="a1" caption="of one accord"
          etymology="अग्नाविष्णू, agni-viṣṇu, vocative case, dual number, O Agni and Viṣṇu.
सजोषसा, sajoṣas, instrumental case, singular number, of one accord.">अग्नाविष्णू सजोषसेमा<w start_time_ms="0" end_time_ms="900">अग्नाविष्णू</w><w start_time_ms="900" end_time_ms="1800">सजोषसेमा</w></line>
    <line start_time_ms="1800" end_time_ms="3400" alignment_id="a2">वर्धन्तु वां गिरः ॥</line>
  </section>
</lyrics>"""

pages, meta = vr_xml_parse(VR)
assert meta['title'] == '॥ श्रीरुद्रचमकप्रश्नः ॥'        # kept as the title
assert not any('श्रीरुद्रचमकप्रश्नः' in t for _, t in pages)   # and dropped from the content

ts = line_times(pages[-1][1])
assert [t.start for t in ts] == [0, 1800] and [t.ms for t in ts] == [1800, 1600]
assert ts[0].aid == 'a1' and ts[0].text == 'अग्नाविष्णू सजोषसेमा'   # `<w>` children stay out of the line
# the corpus writes a whole word-by-word analysis into one attribute, so every physical line needs the
# `> etym:` prefix: an unprefixed continuation line reaches the scansion as if it were a pāda
es = line_etyms(pages[-1][1])
assert len(es) == 2 and es[0].startswith('अग्नाविष्णू,') and es[1].startswith('सजोषसा,')
quoted = lambda pg: all(ln.startswith(('>', '##')) or '[t ' in ln for ln in pg.splitlines() if ln.strip())
assert quoted(pages[-1][1])


VRJ = """{"title": "॥ श्रीरुद्रचमकप्रश्नः ॥", "category": "vedic", "tags": "rudram",
 "sections": [{"name": "anuvaka 1", "meaning": "A dual invocation of Agni and Viṣṇu.",
   "lines": [{"t": "अग्नाविष्णू सजोषसेमा", "s": 0, "e": 1800, "cap": "of one accord",
              "etym": "अग्नाविष्णू, agni-viṣṇu, vocative case, dual number, O Agni and Viṣṇu.\\nसजोषसा, sajoṣas, instrumental case, singular number, of one accord.",
              "w": [["अग्नाविष्णू", 0, 900], ["सजोषसेमा", 900, 1800]]},
             {"t": "वर्धन्तु वां गिरः ॥", "s": 1800, "e": 3400},
             {"t": "[bell]", "role": "audio", "s": 3400, "e": 4000}]}]}"""

pj, mj = vr_json_parse(VRJ)
assert mj['title'] == meta['title'] and mj['category'] == 'vedic'
assert [t.ms for t in line_times(pj[-1][1])] == [1800, 1600]   # `audio` is recited but not printed, so not verse
assert len(line_etyms(pj[-1][1])) == 2                         # one entry per physical line, same as the XML reader
assert quoted(pj[-1][1])
assert sanskrit_parse(VRJ)[1]['fmt'] == 'vedicreader'          # picked by shape, not by extension

text:
deva2iast writes the text in Latin letters keeping vowel length. syllables marks each syllable heavy or light and scan returns that as a g/l string. detect_meter matches it against the tables. A syllable is heavy when its vowel is long or a consonant cluster follows.
fold_token throws vowel length away so a search matches either spelling. Metre needs length, so deva2iast is a second transliteration rather than a reuse of the fold.


source


def deva2iast(
    s:str
)->str:
Devanagari to IAST, keeping the vowel length that scansion depends on.



from ganapati.metre import deva2iast


assert deva2iast('श्रीमाता') == 'śrīmātā'
assert deva2iast('देवी') == 'devī'
assert deva2iast('कर्म') == 'karma'      # the virāma kills the implicit vowel
assert deva2iast('गम्') == 'gam'
assert deva2iast('दे॒वी') == 'devī'      # the Vedic tone mark is stripped first

ai and au are one vowel each, kh and th one consonant each, so atha is two syllables. A consonant closing one syllable does not open the next: in kaṃsa the ṃ belongs to kaṃ.

from ganapati.metre import syllables, scan


assert [s for s, _ in syllables('atha')] == ['a', 'tha']      # `th` is one consonant
assert [s for s, _ in syllables('kaṃsa')] == ['kaṃ', 'sa']    # the ṃ closes the first, not opens the second
assert scan('gam') == 'g'                                     # a final cluster makes it heavy
assert scan('rāma') == 'gl'                                   # long ā, then a bare short a
assert scan('īśā vāsyam idaṃ sarvaṃ') == 'gggllggg'
assert scan(unicodedata.normalize('NFD', 'īśā vāsyam idaṃ sarvaṃ')) == 'gggllggg'   # decomposed IAST keeps its long vowels

text:
Duration against scansion
An aligned source is the one place a scansion can be checked against something outside itself. line_times gives each line’s milliseconds, matras gives its morae, and the two should stay in proportion across a recitation. A line that is far off the chunk’s median is either mis-scanned or mis-aligned. guru_laghu_ratio fits the two durations over many lines; the śāstra says 2:1, and measurement over aligned Vedic recitation lands between 1.3 and 2.7.

def mora_rate(
    text:str
)->float:

from ganapati.text import time_marker


def timed(ps, rate=100):
    'Each pāda with an audio span that honours its morae at `rate` ms per mora.'
    rs = rate if isinstance(rate, list) else [rate] * len(ps)
    out, t = [], 0
    for p, r in zip(ps, rs):
        d = matras(p) * r; out.append(f'{p} {time_marker(t, t + d)}'); t += d
    return '\n'.join(out)

assert mora_rate(timed(padas)) == 100
assert timing_check(timed(padas)) == []
assert 1.99 < guru_laghu_ratio(timed(padas)) < 2.01     # a guru is two laghus, measured
assert timing_check(timed(padas, [100, 100, 100, 180]))[0].start == 8000  # the line out of proportion
assert mora_rate('\n'.join(padas)) is None              # no timings, nothing to measure

title: names
text:
Epithets
EPITHETS holds one group per line: the names a translation writes for a deity or figure, then |, then the epithets a reader may use. The map is one way. Raṅganātha reaches Viṣṇu, Nārāyaṇa and Hari; Viṣṇu does not reach every epithet, so a search for Rāma is not widened to every Rāghava. An epithet two figures share is in both groups (Acyuta, Mādhava). A name that is mostly another word is left out: Śrī, Ramā (Lakṣmī, and rama is Rāma’s key), Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī, and krisna is Kṛṣṇa’s), Guha (Skanda, and the boatman of the Rāmāyaṇa), Kaunteya (any son of Kuntī). Spellings that name_key cannot bring together are listed beside the IAST: Subramanya, Murugan, Bajrangbali.
The names are common knowledge from the epics, the Purāṇas and temple usage, written in IAST.
